scope: Additive selected-policy SHA status field, UI eligibility and displayed selection POST binding; backend selectors and authentication unchanged.
evidence: Backend get_all_versions iterates fixed SERVICES keys; service name used in inline onclick is not a new user-controlled value.
selection_sha256 is a public policy-byte digest, not an authentication secret; selection IDs and digests are validated by release_selection.validate.

submit_job validates the allowlisted service/action/channel, exact optional selection pair, installed policy, enabled component ownership, clear recovery state, current updater capabilities and host-only Proxy adoption before dispatch.
Native selected worker revalidates selection bytes, manifest bytes, admitted artifact digests/platform and source runtime after pulls and before first stop; UI flags do not grant new authority.
Page test exercised real HTML JavaScript and verified selected ID/SHA in POST. Focused independent command returned11PASS in0.46s.

residual_risks.detail: Released baseline nginx /api/update and /api/pull use generic /_auth_check; /auth/headers accepts logged-in readonly sessions, and health-api does not inspect a role. Thus this scoped patch preserves existing authentication behavior but does not establish administrator-only mutation authorization. The endpoint could already be called directly before this change; this is not reported as a newly introduced vulnerability. Do not describe this review as proving an admin-only API.

testing_gaps: GitHub CI, native staging, published payload identity, actual LTX deployment and production browser acceptance were not exercised by this reviewer and remain held.
No claim of security approval for unreleased dev/broker surfaces or full baseline service security.
writes: Only this review-security.json report; no source, publication or runtime changes.
